thread:
sam: flagging a backup/archive problem discovered during a restore test. background-archiver rewrote a set of DB snapshot objects overnight and the new copies lack ServerSideEncryption metadata. seems related to the archiver service account permission change from last week's RBAC cleanup.
anya: how many objects and which buckets? prod or staging?
sam: quick counts: 42 objects in archive-bucket-prod/pg-backups/ from 2025-09-12 02:00-03:30UTC. restores that hit those copies fail decrypt. original copies seem deleted by the rewrite job.
chen: paste from archiver worker log: 
```
2025-09-12T02:17:02Z archiver.worker: rewrite-start key=pg-backups/tenant-22/snap-20250912-0130 size=12GB
2025-09-12T02:17:45Z archiver.worker: rewrite-complete key=pg-backups/tenant-22/snap-20250912-0130 size=12GB dest_etag=abc123
2025-09-12T02:17:45Z archiver.worker: info headers_forwarded={}
```
no SSE info logged.
marcus: RBAC change last week removed kms:Encrypt for the archiver-sa on tenant CMEKs and left only account-level encrypt. If the worker used default account key it should still have SSE metadata, but logs show no headers forwarded. suspect multipart copy path lost metadata when using the low-priv proxy.
anya: do we have access logs showing request headers on the copy?
chen: S3 server access logs show PUTs for the rewrite with no x-amz-server-side-encryption in request_headers for those PUT_COMPLETE events. earlier copies (older than 09/12) do include SSE info.
encops-bot: alert: archive-rewrite-no-sse detected (rule: s3-rewrite-sse-absent). incident ticket ENC-2025-201 opened.
marcus: immediate mitigation: stop archiver job (taken offline), restore originals from tape if available (we have a cold-copy retention for 7 days) or replay from upstream store. also add a validation step: after any rewrite, run head-object and assert ServerSideEncryption present.
anya: compliance/CS: some tenants have contract clauses requiring CMEK on archived backups. we need tenant list and timeline for disclosure. chen, can you run this audit?
chen: running quick query against access logs: 
```
SELECT key, tenant_id, time FROM s3_access_logs
WHERE operation = 'PutObject'
  AND bucket = 'archive-bucket-prod'
  AND time BETWEEN '2025-09-12 02:00' AND '2025-09-12 04:00'
  AND (request_header_x_amz_server_side_encryption IS NULL OR request_header_x_amz_server_side_encryption = '');
```
result: 42 rows. extracting tenant_ids now.
sam: plan of record: 1) archiver offline (done), 2) run per-key head-object to confirm lost metadata (chen), 3) attempt in-place re-encrypt via S3 copy with --metadata-directive REPLACE and --sse-kms-key-id where we have tenant key (marcus/ops), 4) if tenant key not available, restore original or coordinate reupload with tenant.
marcus: small re-encrypt snippet: 
```
aws s3 cp s3://archive-bucket-prod/$key /tmp/$name && \
aws s3 cp /tmp/$name s3://archive-bucket-prod/$key --metadata-directive REPLACE --server-side-encryption aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id $TENANT_KEY_ID
```
chen: note: copying large objects will incur egress and time; prefer server-side copy if possible but need proper permissions. also must record an audit event for every re-encrypt.
anya: create incident timeline, notify legal/compliance/CS with affected tenant list and remediation path. schedule postmortem and RBAC rollback review. thanks team.
encops-bot: ENC-2025-201 created: https://redwood.incidents/ENC-2025-201
